title: Digital Media Forensics joins the Guidewire Marketplace
summary: 1 in 100 claim images Verisk analyzes has suspicious metadata. A new Guidewire Accelerator puts Digital Media Forensics results inside ClaimCenter.
body_markdown:
Manipulated claim media rarely looks manipulated. AI image tools, editing apps, and recycled internet content make it easy to exaggerate damage or fabricate a loss, and everything that documents a claim moves through the same review process: photos, video, invoices, estimates. An adjuster working through hundreds of files a week has little chance of catching a forgery by eye. Digital Media Forensics from Verisk is now available to Guidewire ClaimCenter users through a new accelerator in the Guidewire Marketplace.


## Why is manipulated media in claims so hard to catch?


Manipulation usually leaves a trace in the file, but finding it means reading metadata and comparing one photo against every other image on record. That work doesn’t scale to a full inventory of open claims. Across the claim images, Verisk analyzes:


- **1 in 100** images contains suspicious metadata
- **5 in 1,000** images appear in more than one claim
- **1 in 5,000** images are sourced from the internet


A single reused photo can travel across carriers indefinitely. In one case, Digital Media Forensics matched damage photos from a staged scooter accident across six carriers within a month, all traced back to a Reddit post.


## What does Digital Media Forensics do?


Digital Media Forensics applies automated checks to loss photos and documents submitted with a claim, then returns the findings to the handler. Powered by ClaimSearch®, it flags:


- Images duplicated across claims and across carriers
- Metadata that conflicts with the reported date or location
- Pixel-level manipulation, such as cloned or retouched areas of an image
- AI-generated content, identified through metadata signatures and deepfake metadata indicators
- PDFs, including


Each check is documented, and any referral to the special investigation unit (SIU) carries that evidence with it.


## What does the new Accelerator change?


Connecting ClaimCenter to Digital Media Forensics typically requires custom integration and dedicated IT resources. The Digital Media Forensics Accelerator replaces that work with a pre-built integration directly downloadable from the Guidewire Marketplace.


Forensic results then appear in the claim file in ClaimCenter. Adjusters can review flagged images and documents within their existing workflow, without switching between systems or adding another step to the claim review process.


### Get started


Digital Media Forensics joins more than 30 other Verisk solutions with Guidewire Accelerators. Find it in the[Guidewire Marketplace](https://marketplace.guidewire.com/product/verisk-accelerator-for-digital-media-forensics-for-claimcenter/01tPW00000GcD7tYAF?tab=Media) , or[learn more about Digital Media Forensics](https://www.verisk.com/products/digital-media-forensics/) .


Verisk was also named Marketplace Partner of the Year in the 2025 Guidewire PartnerConnect Technology Excellence Awards, announced at Guidewire Connections in Las Vegas.
